transcript: In my old home stood an ancient piano It had been used by my grandmother in her youth And had the dignity of an antique The keys were yellowed and the tuning was Slightly off But it was our family's treasure Every week my mother would gently wipe the piano And once a year she called a tuner for its maintenance Music is a precious heritage of our family, she said From the age of six, I began lessons on this piano The first few years were bitter, practice seemed silly to me Hearing friends playing outside, I kept repeating scales But in middle school, piano gradually became enjoyable I could play Chopin and Debussy and came to know the joy of expressing my emotions through sound At university I did not select music as my major But I continued playing the piano Even on busy days, the time at the keyboard was my spiritual rest Employment marriage, raising children At every stage of life, the piano was with me on tired nights Sad days, joyful days Music absorbed my feelings and healed me My grandmother passed away, my mother passed away And now it is my daughter who plays the piano My seven-year-old daughter lacks the strength in her fingertips to play Chopin But the sight of her stretching her toes toward the pedal recalls my own image long ago A single old piano has connected the family across four generations An instrument is not a mere object Like a chamber of family history and affection It contains all the memories

segments.text: In my old home stood an ancient piano It had been used by my grandmother in her youth
And had the dignity of an antique The keys were yellowed and the tuning was
Slightly off
But it was our family's treasure
Every week my mother would gently wipe the piano
And once a year she called a tuner for its maintenance
Music is a precious heritage of our family, she said
From the age of six, I began lessons on this piano
The first few years were bitter, practice seemed silly to me
Hearing friends playing outside, I kept repeating scales
But in middle school, piano gradually became enjoyable
I could play Chopin and Debussy and came to know the joy of expressing my emotions through sound
At university I did not select music as my major
But I continued playing the piano
Even on busy days, the time at the keyboard was my spiritual rest
Employment marriage, raising children
At every stage of life, the piano was with me on tired nights
Sad days, joyful days
Music absorbed my feelings and healed me
My grandmother passed away, my mother passed away
And now it is my daughter who plays the piano
My seven-year-old daughter lacks the strength in her fingertips to play Chopin
But the sight of her stretching her toes toward the pedal recalls my own image long ago
A single old piano has connected the family across four generations
An instrument is not a mere object
Like a chamber of family history and affection It contains all the memories
